record.paper_title: Group actions on 4-manifolds: some recent results and open questions
record.context_brief: Upper bounds on prime-order smooth actions
record.original_question: Let X be a smooth 4-manifold that admits no smooth S^1-actions. Does there exist a constant C > 0 such that X admits no nontrivial smooth Z_p-actions for any prime p > C? If such a constant exists, on which structures of X does C depend?

evidence.quote: Question 4.1. (Chen [17]) Let X be a smooth 4-manifold which admits no smooth S1-actions. Does there exist a constant C > 0 such that there are no nontrivial smooth Zp-actions on X for any prime number p > C? Moreover, suppose such a constant C does exist, what structures of X does C depend on?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be a closed smooth 4-manifold that admits no nontrivial smooth action of the circle group S^1. For a prime number p, denote by Z_p the cyclic group of order p, and consider nontrivial smooth actions of Z_p on X.

(a) Does there exist a constant C > 0, depending on X, such that X admits no nontrivial smooth Z_p-action for any prime p > C?

(b) If such a constant C exists, determine on which invariants or structures of X (for instance, the homeomorphism type, the smooth structure, additional geometric structures such as symplectic or complex structures) the constant C depends.
artifact.status_search_result: The general smooth case of the question appears to remain open. Affirmative answers are known under additional structure: W. Chen ("On the orders of periodic diffeomorphisms of 4-manifolds", Duke Math. J. 156 (2011)) established the bound for holomorphic actions (with C of topological nature) and for symplectic actions (with C also depending on the smooth structure). No source found establishes the result for general smooth actions.

status_evidence.title: On the orders of periodic diffeomorphisms of 4-manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: The author gave affirmative results to this question for the case of holomorphic and symplectic actions; the constant C in the holomorphic case is topological in nature, while in the symplectic case it involves also the smooth structure of the manifold.
status_evidence.claim: The question is answered affirmatively in the holomorphic and symplectic settings, with the dependence of C identified, but the general smooth case is not resolved here.
